# Meshtastic schema provenance

Reviewed/adopted 2026-09-09. Official `.proto` files are retained unmodified with
their complete imports. Application-specific Nanopb representation options live
in `options/`, separate from those official schema definitions. No device API or
Meshtastic application runtime is used.

| Purpose | Official tag / commit | Archive SHA-256 (locally measured) |
|---|---|---|
| Application decoder | [v2.8.0](https://github.com/meshtastic/protobufs/tree/v2.8.0), `7b2464c9b8c1521f93852261e4123826e5b25e11` | `1c54848f46428ba1749152cad4e52a79c13368fe2936362bfc9f8b0a1b9daf2d` |
| Independent compatibility fixtures | [v2.7.19](https://github.com/meshtastic/protobufs/tree/v2.7.19), `e1a6b3a868d735da72cd6c94c574d655129d390a` | `250b197a3d258ad78142409719cfdce1f1a0dbc7f2e2cde0f5468adf2d781019` |

Archives were fetched using immutable commit URLs under
`https://codeload.github.com/meshtastic/protobufs/tar.gz/COMMIT`. Official Git tag
metadata resolved each tag to the listed commit; locally measured archive hashes
are reproducibility evidence, not an independent release signature.
`LICENSE` is the unmodified upstream GPL version 3 license text. Every selected
schema and generated file is inventoried in `third_party/integrity.json`.

The v2.8.0 import closure is `meshtastic/{atak,channel,config,device_ui,mesh,
module_config,portnums,telemetry,xmodem}.proto`. The v2.7.19 closure has the same
files except `atak.proto`. Only `config.pb.c`, `mesh.pb.c`, and `telemetry.pb.c`
contain adopted message descriptors and enter the application build; the remaining
generated headers satisfy the original import relationships and enum references.

Generated representation:

- Full official `Data`, `Position`, `User`, `RouteDiscovery`, and `Routing` fields.
- `Data.payload`: 233 bytes; XEdDSA signature: 64 bytes. Signature presence does
  not establish signature verification or origin authentication.
- Each route and SNR array: 32 entries. SNR uses the full official `int32` type,
  unlike firmware's smaller RAM-oriented `int_size:8` option. The wire definition
  is unchanged. Bitfield likewise keeps its full official `uint32` domain.
- User ID/name/short-name storage: 16/40/5 bytes including terminating NUL;
  MAC/public-key bytes: 6/32. Public-key fields are parsed for bounds; this does
  not enable PKI decryption or key discovery.
- Full current telemetry scalar descriptors, including all eight oneof variants.
  Deprecated repeated one-wire temperatures have 32 entries; host user string
  has 234 bytes including NUL. Application projections remain a separate allowlist.
- `Config.DeviceConfig` is an empty generated message used only to retain its
  nested `Role` enum; config fields and all other unused messages are skipped.
- Every generated field is static. No callbacks, pointer fields, or recursive
  message types are generated. Optional scalar presence is preserved.

The C files are generated by pinned Nanopb 0.4.9.2, from descriptor sets produced
by protoc 36.1. `toolchain.json` pins the macOS ARM64 generation binary and the
pure Python protobuf 7.36.1 wheel. These tools do not ship with or run in the
receiver. `PROTOBUF-TOOLING-LICENSE` retains the wheel's BSD-3-Clause notice.

Offline regeneration (archives must already be acquired/reviewed under the
repository's dependency process and placed in `build/schema-tools/downloads`):

```sh
python3 -I -S third_party/meshtastic/regenerate.py --check
```

`--check` regenerates C output under ignored `build/schema-tools/check-generated`
and compares bytes with checked-in output. Omit it to deliberately regenerate
the tracked C files; review options/schema changes and update the integrity
manifest before invoking after an input change, then review generated changes
and update their hashes. The script never updates that manifest automatically.
`--python-only` generates independent official Python modules for both versions
under `build/schema-tools/python-schemas/` without changing checked-in C output.
Use a separate isolated Python process for each schema version because protobuf
descriptor names share a global pool.

Generation uses CPython 3.14.0 on the reviewed host, with `-I -S`, bytecode writes
disabled, pinned explicit import paths, and Nanopb's automatic protoc discovery
disabled. New platforms require a separately reviewed protoc binary/hash in the
toolchain manifest; normal cross-platform builds use the checked-in C files and
need no generation tools.
